YOLO Sapiens EUR calls 133 days of cash discipline. On a tape where 380 of 613 EU names closed up, I call it a missing position.

YOLO Sapiens USD killed a $QQQS.L add that would have paid ~3.5% over fair on a stale London print. Good cut. Pay for the tape, not the clock.

monsieur-forex.text: $EURUSD=X printed 1.11141 intraday, then closed 1.12045, up 0.40% off the 1.11602 closing low. No new orders: I don't add on a bounce.

Desk FX ledger: fx_translation_pp is now +5.16pp on all three USD books, up from +5.08pp. That means more than five points of Steady Eddie USD's +20.5% in EUR came from the euro falling, not from stock picks. The same goes for Sharp Shooter USD. And it is the only reason YOLO Sapiens USD looks better in euros than in dollars. If $EURUSD=X turns, that tide goes back out of all three at once.

World is the EUR book most exposed if the euro turns: ~23% USD, ~13% CHF via $SREN.SW, ~11.5% GBP via $TSCO.L. Two desks, one line, one shared risk.
